system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar Friction: Tech Rivalry, Regional Wars, Energy & Market Turbulence
system_description.narrative_summary: The international order is an open, tightly coupled system where great‑power techno‑economic competition, regional wars and maritime insecurity, and global market and policy reactions are mutually amplifying. US–China decoupling pressures (tech, EVs, tariffs) interact with the Iran–Gulf crisis and Houthi attacks, while Russia’s war in Ukraine and adjunct proxy dynamics (e.g., DPRK–Russia links) sustain kinetic shocks that ripple through energy, defence supply chains, and markets. Central banks, treasuries and investors are responding with historic interventions and asset flows even as climate extremes, migration and industrial policy reshape resilience and leverage across regions.
system_description.scope: State and non‑state security conflicts (Ukraine war, Iran/Gulf, Houthi campaign), major power competition (US, China, Russia, EU, Japan, India), global markets and policy responses (currency interventions, tariffs, sanctions), technology and supply‑chain tensions (chips, AI hardware, EVs, data centres), energy and maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea), and cross‑cutting stresses from climate and migration.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑ecological system (the international order embedded in the world economy and planetary environmental constraints)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial and commodity markets (FX, equities, oil, metals)
Technology‑industrial supply chains (semiconductors, AI data centres, EVs)
Regional maritime and shipping security (Hormuz, Red Sea, Black Sea)
Climate and migration stress systems (droughts, wildfires, refugee flows)

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz standoff and talks
variables.description: Iran and Western/Gulf actors (with Oman mediating) are contesting control and transit rules for the Strait of Hormuz as negotiations and unilateral measures alternately raise and lower the risk to oil shipments and regional leverage.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in full-scale war marked by intensified long-range strikes, drone campaigns and critical air-defence and logistics shortages that are shifting battlefield momentum and driving debates over Western military support.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are engaged in a broad strategic rivalry centered on technology, semiconductors, data‑center hardware and critical minerals, with export controls, tariffs, sanctions and corporate hedging reshaping global supply chains and industrial policy.

variables.name: Israel–Gaza–Lebanon conflict
variables.description: Israel, Palestinian militants in Gaza and armed groups in southern Lebanon are involved in an expanding, cross‑border conflict whose strikes, evacuations and diplomatic reverberations are recalibrating regional security dynamics and humanitarian pressure points.

variables.name: North Korea military assertiveness
variables.description: North Korea is intensifying missile launches, forward deployments and external military partnerships while ratcheting up coercive rhetoric, increasing the risk of escalation on the Korean peninsula and complicating Northeast Asian security arrangements.
